hypothesis: A constraint-guided Quality-Diversity search that preserves multiple viable niches will adapt better to a changed/previously ambiguous goal than a prematurely fixed scalar objective, while using structured search rather than pure random exploration.
baselines: evolution against one fixed scalar interpretation of the initial goal
constraint-guided Quality-Diversity archive across plausible goals
limitations: This is a synthetic toy landscape, not a software-engineering benchmark.
Only one reference random seed is recorded here; no statistical significance claim is made.
The QD strategy is given a set of plausible goals, while the scalar baseline intentionally commits to the initial goal; this encodes the hypothesis rather than proving it.
There are not yet explicit verifier agents, correlated verifier errors, network churn, human-attention cost, or adversarial workers.

The recovery_generations metric is weak in this version because an archive can already contain a strong post-change candidate before the change occurs. Future versions should add regret and adaptation-area metrics.
notes: Local validation of tests/test_emergence_sim.py passed 4 tests before this result was committed.
The reference run is reproducible with: python sim/emergence_sim.py --strategy all --seed 7 --agents 200 --generations 120 --change-at 60 --pretty
